question: In the 1988 Australian Grand Prix, by what percentage was the winner's elapsed time shorter than the last full-distance finisher's? Use the last finisher's time as denominator and round to two decimals.
SQL: WITH finished AS ( SELECT x.positionOrder, x.milliseconds FROM results AS x JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = x.raceId JOIN status AS s ON s.statusId = x.statusId WHERE r.name = 'Australian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 1988 AND s.status = 'Finished' AND x.milliseconds IS NOT NULL ), extremes AS ( SELECT MIN(CASE WHEN positionOrder = 1 THEN milliseconds END) AS winner_ms, MAX(CASE WHEN positionOrder = (SELECT MAX(positionOrder) FROM finished) THEN milliseconds END) AS last_ms FROM finished ) SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (last_ms - winner_ms) / NULLIF(last_ms, 0), 2) FROM extremes

question: What percentage of Japanese-driver race entries from 2007 through 2009 matched their race winner's recorded lap count? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN x.laps = (SELECT y.laps FROM results AS y WHERE y.raceId = x.raceId AND y.positionOrder = 1 ORDER BY y.resultId LIMIT 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) FROM results AS x JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = x.raceId JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverId = x.driverId WHERE d.nationality = 'Japanese' AND r.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009

question: Which 20 drivers recorded the shortest single lap times in Formula 1 races? Give their full names, shortest lap first.
SQL: WITH per_driver AS ( SELECT driverId, MIN(milliseconds) AS fastest_ms FROM lapTimes WHERE milliseconds > 0 GROUP BY driverId ) SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS full_name FROM per_driver AS p JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverId = p.driverId ORDER BY p.fastest_ms, d.driverId LIMIT 20

question: For each Formula 1 circuit in Italy with recorded laps, give the circuit name and its fastest recorded lap time in minutes:seconds.milliseconds format.
SQL: WITH ranked_laps AS (SELECT c.circuitId, c.name AS circuit_name, l.time AS lap_record, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY c.circuitId ORDER BY l.milliseconds, l.raceId, l.driverId, l.lap ) AS rn FROM lapTimes AS l JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = l.raceId JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE c.country = 'Italy' AND l.milliseconds > 0 ) SELECT circuit_name, lap_record FROM ranked_laps WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY circuit_name, circuitId

question: I'm comparing pit stop activity at the newer Grand Prix weekends. Among the 2017 races that were not hosted in 2000, what was the average number of pit stops per race? Please take the average of all of those races and round it to two decimal places.
evidence: Hosted in 2000 means the race was on the 2000 race calendar.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT raceId FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year = 2000)) SELECT ROUND(1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pitStops WHERE raceId IN (SELECT raceId FROM cohort)) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cohort), 2) AS avg_pit_stops_per_race

question: For the 2010 Formula 1 season, how many drivers did Lucas di Grassi qualify ahead of? I want a single number: the count of drivers he out-qualified over the whole season. By 'qualify ahead of' I mean recording a better qualifying position than that driver in the same race, with a lower position number being better. The 2010 season means the races held in the year 2010.
evidence: qualifying position: the starting slot a driver earns in the qualifying session before a race
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T2.driverId) AS drivers_qualified_ahead_of FROM qualifying AS T1 JOIN qualifying AS T2 ON T2.raceId = T1.raceId AND T2.position > T1.position JOIN drivers AS D ON D.driverId = T1.driverId JOIN races AS R ON R.raceId = T1.raceId WHERE D.forename = 'Lucas' AND D.surname = 'di Grassi' AND R.year = 2010;

question: Who won the 2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix? I'd like the winner's forename and surname, the local clock time (hours:minutes:seconds.milliseconds) at the circuit at which he crossed the finish line, and the url of his information page, so I can compare the moment the race ended with the TV coverage.
evidence: A driver's race time is the duration from the start of the race to the moment he crosses the finish line.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, time(r.time, '0' || res.time) || '.' || substr(res.time, -3) AS finish_time, d.url FROM races r JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = res.driverId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Azerbaijan Grand Prix' AND res.positionOrder = 1

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, I'd like to identify the drivers who completed the second qualifying session (Q2) but were knocked out and did not reach Q3. Please list every such driver - no ranking, cutoff or tie-break, just all of them - showing each driver's reference name, nationality and birthday, and nothing else.
evidence: Formula 1 qualifying is run in three timed sessions, Q1, Q2 and Q3; completing a session means the driver recorded a lap time in that session, and only drivers who complete a session move on to the next. The reference name is the driver's short identifier.
SQL: SELECT T2.driverRef, T2.nationality, T2.dob FROM qualifying AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId INNER JOIN races AS R ON T1.raceId = R.raceId WHERE R.year = 2017 AND R.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND T1.q2 IS NOT NULL AND T1.q2 != '' AND (T1.q3 IS NULL OR T1.q3 = '')

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix qualifying, what is the nationality of the driver with the second fastest Q2 time? Only drivers who took part in Q2 count, and by second fastest I mean the second smallest Q2 time. If several drivers share that time, list each of their nationalities.
evidence: Q2 is the second qualifying session of a Grand Prix weekend, after Q1.
SQL: WITH q2times AS (SELECT d.nationality, q.q2 FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 2017 AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2 <> '') SELECT DISTINCT T.nationality FROM q2times T WHERE T.q2 = (SELECT MIN(q2) FROM q2times WHERE q2 > (SELECT MIN(q2) FROM q2times))

question: For qualifying at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, how many drivers set a time in the second qualifying session (Q2) faster than 1:40.000? I just need the count of drivers as a single number.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT q.driverId) AS driver_count FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2 <> '' AND q.q2 < '1:40.000'

question: I'm reviewing the longest service pauses in races across the sport's whole history. Which racetrack saw the longest single pit stop ever? Please give me the racetrack name, location, country, the season year of that race, and the pit stop length. Consider all seasons in the data, and if several pit stops tie for the longest, give me one row for each of them.
evidence: pit stop: a recorded pit-stop entry in a race; pit stop length: how long that pit stop lasted
SQL: SELECT c.name AS racetrack, c.location, c.country, r.year AS season_year, ps.duration AS pit_stop_length FROM pitStops ps JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ps.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE ps.milliseconds = (SELECT MAX(milliseconds) FROM pitStops) ORDER BY c.name

question: I'm putting together a trivia fact about Italian drivers in Formula 1. Who holds the fastest lap time set in Q3 - the third and final part of qualifying - by an Italian driver, across the sport's entire history? Please give me the driver's forename, surname, and the fastest Q3 lap time exactly as it appears in the data. Only consider drivers who have a Q3 lap time recorded for some race, and if several Italian drivers share the exact same fastest Q3 time, list all of them.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of qualifying.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, q.q3 AS q3_time FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE d.nationality = 'Italian' AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 JOIN drivers d2 ON d2.driverId = q2.driverId WHERE d2.nationality = 'Italian' AND q2.q3 > '')

question: I'm writing a piece on the new generation of British Formula 1 talent. Among British F1 drivers born after 1980, who set the fastest Q3 qualifying time, what was that time, and at which race and in which year was it set? Please give me the driver's full name, the race name, the race year, and the Q3 time. By 'born after 1980' I mean the year of birth is later than 1980. If two qualifying results tie for the fastest Q3 time, I'd like a row for each.
evidence: Q3 is the final part of the qualifying session that decides the front of the starting grid.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT q.driverId, q.raceId, q.q3 FROM drivers d JOIN qualifying q ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE d.nationality = 'British' AND CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', d.dob) AS INTEGER) > 1980 AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q.q3) != '') SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name, r.name AS race_name, r.year AS race_year, c.q3 AS q3_time FROM cohort c JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = c.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = c.raceId WHERE c.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM cohort)

question: We're writing a piece on F1's younger generation and want a number for it: how many drivers born in 1976 or later (born from 1 January 1976 onwards) have ever set the second-fastest lap of a race at any point in the history covered by the data? I just need the single count of such drivers.
evidence: By second-fastest lap of a race I mean the driver's own fastest lap in that race was the second quickest among all drivers in that race.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.driverId) AS driver_count FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.dob) >= '1976' AND T1.rank = 2

question: I'm writing a piece about how the same common forenames recur across Formula 1 history. Could you tell me how many different drivers named Peter have ever won a Formula 1 race, and the same for drivers named John? Please give me one count per forename, so I can compare the two — if they turn out to be equal, just report both counts side by side. Nothing else needed.
evidence: A race win means the driver finished first in that race.
SQL: SELECT T1.forename, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.driverId) AS winner_drivers FROM drivers AS T1 INNER JOIN results AS T2 ON T2.driverId = T1.driverId WHERE T2.positionOrder = 1 AND T1.forename IN ('John','Peter') GROUP BY T1.forename ORDER BY T1.forename

question: I'm putting together a historical note on constructor nationalities in Formula 1. For each constructor nationality, how many constructors from that nationality have recorded the fastest lap of a race? Please include every nationality in the result, with a count of 0 for nationalities where no constructor has done so. Count a constructor only when it is officially credited with the quickest single lap time in a race's recorded result - don't compute lap times yourself.
evidence: Fastest lap: the constructor officially credited with the quickest single lap time in a race's recorded result.
SQL: SELECT c.nationality, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.rank = 1 THEN c.constructorId END) AS num_constructors FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN results r ON c.constructorId = r.constructorId GROUP BY c.nationality ORDER BY num_constructors DESC, c.nationality

question: For my monthly recap I need the fastest pit stop made during any F1 race held in September 2016. Please tell me the driver's full name, the pit stop time, the name of the race where it happened, the circuit name, and the circuit location. If two or more pit stops share the fastest time, list each of them with its own driver, race, circuit name and circuit location.
evidence: By pit stop time I mean the elapsed time of a pit stop, from the car arriving at its pit to rejoining the race.
SQL: WITH scope AS (SELECT ps.driverId, ps.duration, ps.milliseconds, r.raceId FROM pitStops ps JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ps.raceId WHERE r.date >= '2016-09-01' AND r.date < '2016-10-01') SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name, s.duration AS pit_stop_time, r.name AS race_name, c.name AS circuit_name, c.location AS circuit_location FROM scope s JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = s.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = s.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE s.milliseconds = (SELECT MIN(milliseconds) FROM scope)

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, which driver set the second-fastest time in the second qualifying session (Q2), and which constructor did he drive for that weekend? By second-fastest I mean the driver whose Q2 time comes next after the quickest one, counting every driver who took part in that session. If two drivers tie on Q2 time, the one who started the race higher up the grid counts as the faster of the two. Please give me the driver's forename, the driver's surname, and the constructor name.
evidence: Q2: the second of the weekend's qualifying sessions; its times are measured to the thousandth of a second.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT d.driverId, d.forename, d.surname, co.name AS constructor, q.q2, q.position, CAST(SUBSTR(q.q2, 1, INSTR(q.q2, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) AS mins, CAST(SUBSTR(q.q2, INSTR(q.q2, ':') + 1) AS REAL) AS secs FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId JOIN constructors co ON co.constructorId = q.constructorId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2 <> '') SELECT forename, surname, constructor FROM t ORDER BY mins ASC, secs ASC, position ASC, driverId ASC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1

question: I'm writing a season review piece and need the outright quickest Q2 time of the 2017 Formula One season – the fastest single Q2 time set at any race that year. Please give me the surname of the driver who set it and the name of the race where it was set. If two drivers share that fastest Q2 time, list every one of them along with the race names.
evidence: Q2: the second of the three qualifying sessions of a Grand Prix weekend.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT d.surname AS surname, r.name AS race_name, q.driverId AS driverId, q.q2 AS q2 FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND q.q2 LIKE '%:%.%'), m AS (SELECT MIN(q2) AS q2 FROM t) SELECT t.surname, t.race_name FROM t JOIN m ON m.q2 = t.q2 ORDER BY t.driverId ASC

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, who set the fastest lap time in Q3 (the final qualifying session), and what was that time? Give me the driver code along with the fastest Q3 time. If two or more drivers tie for the fastest Q3 time, list every tied driver.
evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session; a driver's Q3 time is the lap time that driver set in that session
SQL: SELECT T2.code, T1.q3 FROM qualifying AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 ON T2.driverId = T1.driverId WHERE T1.raceId = (SELECT raceId FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND name = 'Italian Grand Prix') AND T1.q3 <> '' AND T1.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE raceId = (SELECT raceId FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND name = 'Italian Grand Prix') AND q3 <> '')

question: Which Chinese Grand Prix edition from the 2000s (2000–2009 seasons) had the earliest scheduled local start time? Give me the season year of that edition and the runner-up's time gap to the winner (the runner-up being the driver classified second at the finish). If several editions share the earliest scheduled local start time, use the most recent one.
evidence: Scheduled local start time: the time of day the race was scheduled to start, local to the circuit.
SQL: SELECT r.year, res.time AS runner_up_gap FROM races r JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId WHERE r.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND r.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2009 AND res.positionOrder = 2 AND r.time IS NOT NULL AND r.time = (SELECT MIN(r2.time) FROM races r2 WHERE r2.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND r2.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2009 AND r2.time IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY r.year DESC LIMIT 1

question: I'm writing a retrospective on the 2017 Italian Grand Prix at Monza. For the Q3 session of that race's qualifying, can you give me the permanent career race number and surname of every driver whose Q3 lap time was strictly faster than 1 minute 38.000 seconds? I want all drivers under that mark, not just the fastest, and no particular order. Note that by permanent career race number I mean the number a driver carries throughout his career, not a one-off entry number for that weekend.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final qualifying session; a driver only has a Q3 time if he actually took part in that session.
SQL: WITH mark(t) AS (SELECT '1' || ':' || '38.000') SELECT d.number, d.surname FROM qualifying AS q INNER JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = q.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 LIKE '%:%' AND q.q3 < (SELECT t FROM mark) ORDER BY d.number;

question: Across all seasons in the database, which circuit's Grand Prix started earliest in the day, and which started latest? I'd like the circuit reference name of the earliest one, the circuit reference name of the latest one, and the gap between those two start times in seconds. Include every season, and if several circuits share the earliest start time, list them all - same for the latest.
evidence: By "start time of the day" I mean the local clock time at the venue at which the race started.
SQL: WITH per_circuit AS (SELECT c.circuitRef AS circuitRef, MIN(CAST(strftime('%s', r.time) AS INTEGER)) AS earliest_start_seconds, MAX(CAST(strftime('%s', r.time) AS INTEGER)) AS latest_start_seconds FROM races r JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE r.time IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.circuitRef) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(circuitRef, ', ') AS earliest_circuitRef, (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(circuitRef, ', ') FROM per_circuit WHERE latest_start_seconds = (SELECT MAX(latest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit)) AS latest_circuitRef, (SELECT MAX(latest_start_seconds) - MIN(earliest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit) AS gap_seconds FROM per_circuit WHERE earliest_start_seconds = (SELECT MIN(earliest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit)

question: For my retrospective on the 1962 British Grand Prix – the race named 'British Grand Prix' in the 1962 season – how many drivers withdrew from that race? I just need a single whole number.
evidence: A driver who withdrew from a race is recorded with the status 'Withdrew'.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT x.driverId) AS num_withdrawn_drivers FROM results AS x JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = x.raceId JOIN status AS s ON s.statusId = x.statusId WHERE r.name = 'British Grand Prix' AND r.year = 1962 AND s.status = 'Withdrew'

question: For the 1957 British Grand Prix, what percentage of the drivers who took part in the race were classified finishers, rounded to two decimals? By classified finisher I mean a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner. I just need the one percentage figure.
evidence: classified finisher: a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner
SQL: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.position IS NOT NULL THEN x.driverId END) / COUNT(DISTINCT x.driverId), 2) AS finisher_percentage FROM races r JOIN results x ON x.raceId = r.raceId WHERE r.year = 1957 AND r.name = 'British Grand Prix'

question: What was Elijah Allen's mean total expense per event for expenses dated in September or October? Round to two decimals.
SQL: WITH per_event AS ( SELECT b.link_to_event, SUM(e.cost) AS event_spend FROM expense AS e JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member JOIN budget AS b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget WHERE m.first_name = 'Elijah' AND m.last_name = 'Allen' AND SUBSTR(e.expense_date, 6, 2) IN ('09','10') AND b.link_to_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.link_to_event ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(event_spend), 2) FROM per_event

question: What is the total amount spent on Student Club events in 2019 minus the total spent on events in 2020?
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTR(T1.event_date, 1, 4) = '2019' THEN T2.spent ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTR(T1.event_date, 1, 4) = '2020' THEN T2.spent ELSE 0 END) AS num FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event

question: List the name of students that have attended more than 7 events.
SQL: SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN attendance AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member GROUP BY T2.link_to_member HAVING COUNT(T2.link_to_event) > 7

question: Which members incurred at least one expense above the overall average expense cost? Give each member's first name, last name, and phone number as separate fields.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T3.first_name, T3.last_name, T3.phone FROM expense AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.link_to_budget = T2.budget_id INNER JOIN member AS T3 ON T3.member_id = T1.link_to_member WHERE T1.cost > ( SELECT AVG(T1.cost) FROM expense AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.link_to_budget = T2.budget_id INNER JOIN member AS T3 ON T3.member_id = T1.link_to_member )

question: I'm reviewing our roster against the catalog and want to see how much of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences' coverage our members actually hold, department by department. For each department in that college, give me: the department's name, the majors it offers, the majors held by at least one of our members, and the average members per major it offers, rounded to two decimals. Membership is as currently listed in the member records, and count a department as belonging to the college when any of its majors sits in the college.
evidence: College of Humanities and Social Sciences: one of the colleges that houses departments offering majors.
SQL: SELECT m.department, COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id) AS majors_offered, COUNT(DISTINCT mem.link_to_major) AS majors_held, ROUND(1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT mem.member_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id), 2) AS avg_members_per_major FROM major m LEFT JOIN member mem ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id WHERE m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' GROUP BY m.department

question: I'm putting together our yearly report and need a breakdown of our 2019 events by event type. For each type of event we held in 2019, please give me: the event type, how many members attended that type's events during 2019, and the total amount budgeted for that type's events in dollars. A few notes: 2019 means the calendar year; the budgeted amount is the planned amount, not what was actually spent. If nothing was budgeted for a type's events, or no member attended them, just show zero. Please list one row per event type, in alphabetical order by event type.
SQL: SELECT e.type AS event_type, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a JOIN event e2 ON e2.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE e2.type = e.type AND SUBSTR(e2.event_date, 1, 4) = '2019') AS members_who_attended, CAST(COALESCE((SELECT SUM(b.amount) FROM budget b JOIN event e3 ON e3.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE e3.type = e.type AND SUBSTR(e3.event_date, 1, 4) = '2019'), 0) AS REAL) AS total_budgeted FROM event e WHERE SUBSTR(e.event_date, 1, 4) = '2019' GROUP BY e.type ORDER BY e.type

question: I'm putting together a financial overview for the college that houses the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department. For each department of that college, can you tell me the total dues the club actually received from that department's enrolled members who took part in the club's events, in dollars? Please include every department of the college, showing zero if we received no such dues from it. Just the department name and the total dues per department.
evidence: 'Dues' is the income source label for membership dues a member pays to the club; 'Member' is the club position of an enrolled member, as opposed to officer or inactive positions.
SQL: SELECT m.department, COALESCE(SUM(i.amount), 0) AS total_dues_received FROM major AS m LEFT JOIN member AS mb ON mb.link_to_major = m.major_id AND mb.position = 'Member' LEFT JOIN income AS i ON i.link_to_member = mb.member_id AND i.source = 'Dues' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attendance AS a WHERE a.link_to_member = mb.member_id) WHERE m.college IN (SELECT college FROM major WHERE department = 'Electrical and Computer Engineering Department') GROUP BY m.department ORDER BY m.department;

question: For the mid-year budget review: I need to see, for each member who had to spend more than fifty dollars on an expense, how much room was still left in the budget lines those purchases were charged against. Please give me, per member, their first name, last name, and the total amount left across those budget lines in dollars rounded to two decimals. Order the results from the largest total down to the smallest; if two members have the same total, list them alphabetically by last name and then first name. The totals should cover all expenses on record, and if a budget line ended up overdrawn, its negative remaining amount should count toward the total.
evidence: Spending more than fifty dollars on an expense means the expense's dollar cost is over 50. The amount left in a budget line is the amount budgeted for that line minus the amount spent against it.
SQL: SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name, ROUND(SUM(b.remaining), 2) AS remaining_total FROM member AS m JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_member, link_to_budget FROM expense WHERE cost > 50) AS e ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN budget AS b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget GROUP BY m.member_id, m.first_name, m.last_name ORDER BY remaining_total DESC, m.last_name ASC, m.first_name ASC

question: How many majors offered by the college that offers Tyler Hewitt's major currently have no enrolled members in the club? Count every major that college offers, by major name.
evidence: Enrolled members are the people recorded in the club's membership list.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_majors_without_members FROM major AS m WHERE m.college = (SELECT T2.college FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id WHERE T1.first_name = 'Tyler' AND T1.last_name = 'Hewitt') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member AS mm WHERE mm.link_to_major = m.major_id)

question: For every budget review event the club has held, can you give me the event name, its location, and the number of members who attended? I need this for the year-end report.
evidence: 'Budget' is the club's event type for its budget review events, such as the Fall Budget Review and the Spring Budget Review.
SQL: SELECT e.event_name, e.location, COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS attended FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE e.type = 'Budget' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name, e.location

question: I'm planning study-partner pairings around our biggest social-attendance event. Can you tell me which academic majors were most represented among the members who attended the football game? For each major, give me the major name and the number of attendees in that major. If several majors tie for the highest attendee count, list all of them, ordered alphabetically by major name.
evidence: Football game: the event named 'Football game'
SQL: WITH cnt AS (SELECT mj.major_name AS major_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS attendees FROM event e JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major WHERE e.event_name = 'Football game' GROUP BY mj.major_id, mj.major_name) SELECT major_name, attendees FROM cnt WHERE attendees = (SELECT MAX(attendees) FROM cnt) ORDER BY major_name

question: I want to gauge how much of the university's range of academic programs our club is failing to reach. Out of every major offered by the university - including majors where we have no members - what percentage have no club member studying them? Please give me just that single percentage, between 0 and 100, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Major: an academic program offered by the university, as listed in the club's records of majors.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major AS m WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member AS mem WHERE mem.link_to_major = m.major_id)) AS REAL) * 100 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major), 2) AS percentage

question: I'm finalizing the semester wrap-up report and need one number: how many different kinds of things the club bought for events that went over budget this semester. A few things to keep in mind: an event counts as over budget if, in at least one of its budgeted categories, we spent more than we budgeted for that category - the budgeted amount minus what was actually spent came out below zero. Also, a single purchase can cover several kinds of things at once, and the purchase description lists what it bought, so make sure each kind is counted. The answer should cover the whole semester shown in the records, and I just need the single integer count, nothing else.
evidence: went over budget: a budgeted category of the event ended with more spent than was budgeted for it, i.e. the amount budgeted minus the amount spent is below zero; kind of thing: a type of item bought, like water, pizza or posters
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE over_budget_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE amount - spent < 0), purchases AS (SELECT ex.expense_description AS d FROM expense ex JOIN budget b ON ex.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM over_budget_events)), items(item, rest) AS (SELECT TRIM(SUBSTR(d || ',', 1, INSTR(d || ',', ',') - 1)), SUBSTR(d || ',', INSTR(d || ',', ',') + 1) FROM purchases UNION ALL SELECT TRIM(SUBSTR(rest, 1, INSTR(rest, ',') - 1)), SUBSTR(rest, INSTR(rest, ',') + 1) FROM items WHERE rest <> '') SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT LOWER(item)) AS kinds FROM items WHERE item <> ''

question: For every event in our records that had at least one attendee, I need the amount spent per attendee on bottled drinking water, in dollars and cents rounded to two decimals. Give me one row per event with the event name and that amount; if an attended event had no water purchases, show 0.00, and if two events share a name, list them separately. Include all events regardless of status, across the club's entire history. A purchase that included water along with other items counts fully toward water.
evidence: water: bottled drinking water bought for attendees
SQL: WITH water AS (SELECT b.link_to_event AS event_id, SUM(e.cost) AS total_cost FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE e.expense_description LIKE '%water%' GROUP BY b.link_to_event), att AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS attendees FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT ev.event_name, ROUND(COALESCE(w.total_cost, 0) / a.attendees, 2) AS water_cost_per_attendee FROM event ev JOIN att a ON a.event_id = ev.event_id LEFT JOIN water w ON w.event_id = ev.event_id GROUP BY ev.event_id, ev.event_name, a.attendees, w.total_cost ORDER BY ev.event_name

question: For my report on the club's academic makeup, could you tell me how many members on the club roster major in a department of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, and how many members do not? The two counts together should cover every member on the roster, with each member counted in exactly one of the two groups. A member counts as majoring in the college only if the department offering their major belongs to the College of Humanities and Social Sciences.
evidence: The College of Humanities and Social Sciences is a college made up of certain departments; membership in the college is determined by which department offers a member's major.
SQL: WITH flag AS (SELECT m.member_id, CASE WHEN b.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS in_college FROM member m LEFT JOIN major b ON m.link_to_major = b.major_id) SELECT SUM(in_college) AS members_in_college, COUNT(*) - SUM(in_college) AS members_not_in_college FROM flag

question: For our snack budget planning: among the events that spent money on chips, which event has the highest budget amount? By budget amount I mean a single budget line, not a total across lines - compare events by their largest single budgeted line. If several events tie on that largest line, list all of their names. Please just give me the event name(s).
SQL: WITH chip_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT b.link_to_event AS event_id FROM budget AS b INNER JOIN expense AS x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE x.expense_description LIKE '%chips%') SELECT e.event_name FROM event AS e INNER JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT event_id FROM chip_events) AND b.amount = (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM budget WHERE link_to_event IN (SELECT event_id FROM chip_events))

question: I'm reviewing member engagement for our club's events in MU 215. Can you give me, for each event category of events held at MU 215, the number of club members who attended those events? Please count events regardless of their status (planning, open, or closed), and make sure every category that had events at MU 215 shows up, even if none of its events had any attendees.
evidence: MU 215: the room name as the event location.
SQL: SELECT e.type AS event_category, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attended_members FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.location = 'MU 215' GROUP BY e.type

question: I'm putting together a recruitment report for the colleges and want to know which parts of the university our club's membership actually draws from. For every person on the roster-regardless of their position in the club-look at their major, and the college that houses the department offering that major. Which college or colleges do the most majors on our roster come from, and how many majors is that? If there's a tie at the top, give me every college tied at that count. Please list the colleges in alphabetical order by college name, and return just each college's name and its number of majors.
evidence: Major: a field of study offered by a department housed in a college.
SQL: WITH cnt AS (SELECT mj.college AS college, COUNT(DISTINCT mj.major_id) AS majors FROM member m JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major GROUP BY mj.college) SELECT college, majors FROM cnt WHERE majors = (SELECT MAX(majors) FROM cnt) ORDER BY college

question: I want to review what the money actually went on for the well-funded events, by venue. For events that had a budget line of more than forty dollars, how many different things were bought for them at each location? Please give me, for each location, the location of the event and the number of different things bought for such events at that location, and nothing else. Note that a budget line of more than forty dollars means a single budgeted amount strictly over 40 dollars, and all qualifying events held at a location should be pooled together.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split(item, rest, loc) AS (SELECT '', x.expense_description || ',', e.location FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = x.link_to_budget JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.amount > 40 UNION ALL SELECT trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)), substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1), loc FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT loc AS location, COUNT(DISTINCT item) AS things_bought FROM split WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY loc ORDER BY loc

question: Hi - I need one overall figure for the budget next year: what's the average total amount we've actually spent per event, counting all budget categories, across every event we've ever recorded? Please give me the average in dollars, rounded to two decimal places, with no date restriction.
SQL: WITH per_event AS (SELECT e.event_id, COALESCE(SUM(b.spent), 0) AS total_spent FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id) SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_spent), 2) AS average_total_spent_per_event FROM per_event

question: For our year-end review, I want to know which event formats bring in the most people. Looking at our whole club year (every event from September 2019 through May 2020), which event type was attended by the most members, and how many members attended that type's events? If several event types tie for the most, list every one of them. Just give me the event type and the number of members for it - nothing else.
evidence: By "attended" I mean a member coming to an event; event type is the kind of event, e.g. Meeting, Social, Game, Election, Community Service.
SQL: WITH member_counts AS (SELECT e.type AS event_type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.type) SELECT event_type, members FROM member_counts WHERE members = (SELECT MAX(members) FROM member_counts) ORDER BY event_type

question: I'm putting together next semester's purchasing plan and want to know which food and drink item the club buys most often. Among purchases made under the food budget only, which single item appears on the most purchase records, and how many purchase records mention it? If two items are tied, go with the one whose name comes first alphabetically. Please give me just the item's name and that record count.
evidence: A purchase record is an entry in the club's expense records for money spent on a purchase.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE items(expense_id, item, rest) AS (SELECT e.expense_id, '', e.expense_description || ',' FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.category = 'Food' UNION ALL SELECT expense_id, trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)), substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1) FROM items WHERE rest <> '') SELECT item AS item_name, COUNT(DISTINCT expense_id) AS record_count FROM items WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY item ORDER BY record_count DESC, item LIMIT 1

question: I'm wrapping up the October Meeting and need the final numbers broken down by what we actually bought, not just by budget category. For every item bought with approved money for the October Meeting, can you give me: the item's name, the budget category of the purchase that included the item, and the total cost in dollars of the approved October Meeting purchases that included the item? Only expenses marked as approved count - an expense without an approval mark doesn't. If an item was included in approved purchases recorded under more than one budget category, give me one row per category. Costs should be plain sums in US dollars with no rounding, and please sort the list by category and then by item name.
evidence: An item is a single thing bought with club money, such as water, pizza or posters. A purchase is an expense recorded for the event.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split AS (SELECT link_to_budget AS bid, cost, '' AS item, expense_description || ',' AS rest FROM expense WHERE approved = 'true' UNION ALL SELECT bid, cost, trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)), substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT s.item AS item, b.category AS category, SUM(s.cost) AS total_cost FROM split s JOIN budget b ON s.bid = b.budget_id JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE s.item <> '' AND e.event_name = 'October Meeting' GROUP BY s.item, b.category ORDER BY b.category, s.item

question: I'm preparing the year-end audit of club spending. For each item Sacha Harrison bought with club money, I need the item name and how many times she bought it. Can you give me that list?
evidence: By "item" I mean an individual thing named in a record of what money was spent for.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split(rest, item) AS (SELECT expense_description || ',', '' FROM expense WHERE link_to_member = (SELECT member_id FROM member WHERE first_name = 'Sacha' AND last_name = 'Harrison') UNION ALL SELECT substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1), trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)) FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT item, COUNT(*) AS times FROM split WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY item ORDER BY item

question: For our department report, I need to know how many different fields of study our club members from the Political Science Department represent. Only count members of the Political Science Department - members from other departments don't count. Just give me the number of different majors studied by those members.
evidence: A major is a field of study offered by a department.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T2.major_id) AS different_majors FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id WHERE T2.department = 'Political Science Department'

question: Among Marvel Comics superheroes with a known eye colour, rank the eye colours by number of superheroes. Give each colour, its hero count, and its rank, most common first; break display-order ties alphabetically.
SQL: WITH colour_counts AS (SELECT c.colour AS eye_colour, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = s.eye_colour_id JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND c.colour <> 'No Colour' GROUP BY c.colour) SELECT eye_colour, hero_count, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY hero_count DESC) AS popularity_rank FROM colour_counts ORDER BY hero_count DESC, eye_colour

question: List the superheroes from Marvel Comics who have the super power of 'Super Strength'.
SQL: SELECT superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS T2 INNER JOIN superpower AS T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id WHERE T3.power_name = 'Super Strength' AND T1.id = T2.hero_id)AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS T4 WHERE T4.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND T1.publisher_id = T4.id)

question: Among all superheroes with recorded height from 150 through 180 cm, what percentage were published by Marvel Comics? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE s.height_cm BETWEEN 150 AND 180

question: What known full names belong to superheroes tied for the highest strength attribute value?
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT s.full_name FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND ha.attribute_value = ( SELECT MAX(ha2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute AS ha2 JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Strength' ) AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' ORDER BY s.full_name ASC

question: List superheroes whose known eye, hair and skin colours are all the same, along with any recorded publisher name.
SQL: SELECT s.superhero_name, p.publisher_name FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = s.eye_colour_id WHERE s.eye_colour_id = s.hair_colour_id AND s.eye_colour_id = s.skin_colour_id AND c.colour <> 'No Colour'

question: Which publisher has more superheroes, DC Comics or Marvel Comics, and by how many? Return Tie if their counts are equal.
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dc, SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS marvel FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id) SELECT CASE WHEN dc > marvel THEN 'DC Comics' WHEN marvel > dc THEN 'Marvel Comics' ELSE 'Tie' END, ABS(dc - marvel) FROM counts

question: I'm comparing Marvel and DC rosters and want to quantify how tall Marvel's roster is for characters whose abilities DC cannot match. What is the average height, in centimetres, of Marvel Comics characters who have at least one power that no DC Comics character has? Only characters with a measured height count.
evidence: A "power" is any single ability listed for a character in the database.
SQL: SELECT AVG(s.height_cm) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND s.height_cm > 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp2 JOIN superhero AS s2 ON s2.id = hp2.hero_id JOIN publisher AS p2 ON p2.id = s2.publisher_id WHERE p2.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND hp2.power_id = hp.power_id))

question: For a segment on strength heroes, I want to know how many superpowers are held only by heroes who have Super Strength. A power counts as held only if at least one hero who has Super Strength holds it, and Super Strength itself should be included if it meets that condition. Just give me the count.
evidence: Super Strength is a super power name.
SQL: WITH strength_heroes AS (SELECT hp.hero_id FROM hero_power AS hp INNER JOIN superpower AS sp ON hp.power_id = sp.id WHERE sp.power_name = 'Super Strength') SELECT COUNT(*) AS power_count FROM superpower AS s WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.power_id = s.id AND hp.hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM strength_heroes)) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp2 WHERE hp2.power_id = s.id AND hp2.hero_id NOT IN (SELECT hero_id FROM strength_heroes))

question: For my 'giants of the genre' feature, I want to headline how varied the abilities of the tallest heroes are. How many different superpowers appear among the ten tallest superheroes? Rank heroes by height and take the top ten; if several heroes tie at the tenth-tallest height, include all of them. A hero counts among the ten tallest even if no powers are on file for them. Please give me just that single number.
evidence: superpower = an ability such as Agility or Accelerated Healing, as named in the superpower list
SQL: WITH top10 AS (SELECT id FROM superhero ORDER BY height_cm DESC LIMIT 10) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T3.power_name) AS superpowers FROM top10 JOIN hero_power T2 ON top10.id = T2.hero_id JOIN superpower T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id

question: Hey, following up on my count of the God / Eternal heroes – among those who are male, what's the average number of superpowers per hero? Just give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: A superpower is any power linked to a hero.
SQL: WITH power_counts AS (SELECT s.id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) AS power_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id WHERE r.race = 'God / Eternal' AND g.gender = 'Male') SELECT ROUND(AVG(power_count), 2) AS average_superpowers FROM power_counts

question: For my cryokinesis page, I want to know how broad the power portfolios are around ice-powered heroes. Consider all heroes who share at least one superpower with a cryokinesis holder - including the cryokinesis holders themselves, since they share cryokinesis with each other. What is the average number of superpowers these heroes have, rounded to one decimal place? Please send back just that single number.
evidence: Cryokinesis is the superpower to generate and control ice.
SQL: WITH sharers AS (SELECT DISTINCT hp2.hero_id FROM hero_power hp1 JOIN hero_power hp2 ON hp2.power_id = hp1.power_id WHERE hp1.hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id = (SELECT id FROM superpower WHERE power_name = 'Cryokinesis'))), counts AS (SELECT hero_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM sharers) GROUP BY hero_id) SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt), 1) AS avg_superpower_count FROM counts

question: I'm researching heroes like A-Bomb. What is the average height in centimetres of the superheroes in A-Bomb's group? Please give me just that single number, rounded to one decimal place. Note that A-Bomb itself belongs to its group and should be included, and only heroes whose height is actually on record should count toward the average-anyone without a recorded height should be left out rather than counted as some height.
evidence: In this request, "group" refers to race.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN height_cm > 0 THEN height_cm END), 1) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero WHERE race_id = (SELECT race_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb')

question: I'm writing a piece about which real publishing companies have put out very tall heroes. How many publishers in the database have released at least one hero taller than 200 cm? Note that taller than 200 cm means strictly more than 200 cm, and it counts if even one of their heroes is that tall. I just need the number of publishers, nothing else.
evidence: A hero's publisher being 'released' means the publisher the hero is attributed to in the database.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.publisher_id) AS publisher_count FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN publisher AS T2 ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id WHERE T1.height_cm > 200 AND T2.publisher_name <> ''

question: For a licensing survey of non-DC heroic characters, I need a single total count of superheroes whose alignment is Good and who are not published by DC Comics. Just that one number, please.
evidence: Good means the hero's alignment is Good; DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN alignment AS T2 ON T1.alignment_id = T2.id WHERE T2.alignment = 'Good' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS T3 WHERE T3.id = T1.publisher_id AND T3.publisher_name = 'DC Comics')

question: I'm comparing superhero body weights to typical human weights for an article. What is the average weight in kilograms of superheroes published by DC Comics, rounded to one decimal place, and how many DC Comics superheroes is that average based on? Only superheroes with a known weight should count toward the average, so the count should be the number of superheroes it's based on. DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 1) AS avg_weight_kg, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND s.weight_kg > 0

question: I'm comparing how power-rich male and female heroes are. For all male heroes and all female heroes that have a documented real full name, what is the average number of superpowers per hero for each gender? Please compute each average over the entire hero population of that gender, not just the heroes that happen to have power records. Give me both averages, each rounded to two decimal places, and nothing else.
evidence: Full name: the hero's real, full personal name (first name plus last name, and optionally middle names); single names such as mononyms or aliases are not a full name.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 2) AS avg_superpowers_male, ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 2) AS avg_superpowers_female FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id LEFT JOIN (SELECT hero_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hero_power GROUP BY hero_id) AS pc ON pc.hero_id = s.id WHERE s.full_name LIKE '% %'

question: I'm putting together a physical profile of the green-skinned villain corner of the universe for a fan wiki page. Could you tell me the average height in centimetres and the average weight in kilograms of the green-skinned villains? Please average only over the characters whose measurement is actually on record - a character with no recorded height or weight shouldn't drag the average down - and round each average to two decimals. I just need those two numbers.
evidence: By 'villain' I mean a character whose alignment is Bad, and by 'green-skinned' I mean a character whose skin colour is Green. Height in centimetres and weight in kilograms are the character's height_cm and weight_kg as commonly understood physical measurements.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN T1.height_cm > 0 THEN T1.height_cm END), 2) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN T1.weight_kg > 0 THEN T1.weight_kg END), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN alignment AS T2 ON T1.alignment_id = T2.id INNER JOIN colour AS T3 ON T1.skin_colour_id = T3.id WHERE T2.alignment = 'Bad' AND T3.colour = 'Green'

question: I'm writing an article about green-skinned flying villains and need a body-statistics fact. What is the average weight, in kilograms, of all green-skinned villains who can fly? By villain I mean a character whose moral affiliation is Bad. Please include only characters whose weight was actually measured-any character whose weight was never measured should be left out of the average. Give me just the single number, rounded to the nearest kilogram.
evidence: Flight: the power to fly.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END)) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN alignment AS a ON s.alignment_id = a.id INNER JOIN colour AS c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id INNER JOIN hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id INNER JOIN superpower AS sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id WHERE a.alignment = 'Bad' AND c.colour = 'Green' AND sp.power_name = 'Flight'

question: I'm doing a physical-profile breakdown of the George Lucas catalogue. For the heroes published by George Lucas that have at least one superpower in the database, what is their average weight in kilograms, counting only the heroes whose weight is recorded? Please give me just that one number, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: George Lucas refers to the publisher name.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id)

question: For the article I'm writing on heroic female characters, I'd like a physique stat for the trivia box: what is the average weight in kilograms of female superheroes whose alignment is good? Only count superheroes whose weight is known. Please round the result to two decimal places.
evidence: Alignment: the superhero's moral category, e.g. good, bad, neutral.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id JOIN alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND a.alignment = 'Good' AND s.weight_kg > 0

question: I'm picking powers for a lightweight male hero archetype. How many different superpowers are held by at least one male superhero who weighs under 70 kilograms? Heroes whose weight isn't recorded shouldn't count as weighing under 70.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS power_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id JOIN superpower AS sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.weight_kg < 70;

question: I want to know about the lightest superhero whose weight has actually been recorded. Among all heroes sharing that lightest weight, give me the largest number of superpowers any of them has. If such a hero has no powers, that counts as 0. Please return just that one number.
evidence: A superpower is one power a hero has, identified by its name.
SQL: SELECT MAX(cnt) AS power_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(hp.power_id) AS cnt FROM superhero AS h LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON h.id = hp.hero_id WHERE h.weight_kg = (SELECT MIN(weight_kg) FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg > 0) GROUP BY h.id)

question: I'm preparing a report on Marvel's roster and want to gauge how heroic their catalogued heroes are. Among Marvel Comics superheroes whose civilian full name is documented, what percentage are good? Please give me just that single percentage, rounded to two decimal places. Note: the percentage should be taken over all Marvel Comics superheroes with a known full name - those whose moral alignment is unknown still count toward the total, just not as good.
evidence: Good refers to alignment = 'Good'. A full name means the hero's real-world civilian identity, i.e. an actual person's name such as 'Charles Chandler' or 'Richard Milhouse Jones'.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T3.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*), 2) AS percentage FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN publisher AS T2 ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id LEFT JOIN alignment AS T3 ON T1.alignment_id = T3.id WHERE T2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND T1.full_name IS NOT NULL AND T1.full_name <> '-'

question: What percentage of Marvel Comics superheroes with a recorded superpower are classified as good? Round the percentage to two decimal places, and give me just that single value.
evidence: Good means alignment 'Good'; superpower refers to a hero's recorded power.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*), 2) AS good_percentage FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id LEFT JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id)

question: I'm comparing the builds of heroes whose power sets overlap with 3-D Man's. What is the average weight in kg of the heroes other than 3-D Man that share at least one superpower with him? Please round it to two decimal places, leave out any heroes whose weight isn't recorded, and return just that single number.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight_kg), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name <> '3-D Man' AND weight_kg > 0 AND id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id = (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = '3-D Man')))

question: How many distinct patients with a triglyceride result of at least 200 were older than 50 on 2026-10-09?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient AS p WHERE p.Birthday < '1976-10-09' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.TG >= 200)

question: How many distinct patients have at least one positive CRP laboratory result and no recorded patient description?
evidence: Plus-marked CRP results indicate positivity.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.CRP LIKE '%+' AND p.Description IS NULL

question: Among the lab tests with the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein result (i.e., the highest result value), find the highest total bilirubin level and give me that test's total bilirubin level, the date of the lab test, the patient's ID, sex, and birthday. If several of those tests share the highest total bilirubin level, list each of them, one row per test.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the anti-RNP antibody lab test; total bilirubin refers to the total serum bilirubin lab test (a liver marker).
SQL: SELECT T2.`T-BIL`, T2.`Date`, T1.ID, T1.SEX, T1.Birthday FROM `Patient` AS T1 INNER JOIN `Laboratory` AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE CAST(T2.`RNP` AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(`RNP` AS REAL)) FROM `Laboratory`) AND T2.`T-BIL` = (SELECT MAX(`T-BIL`) FROM `Laboratory` WHERE CAST(`RNP` AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(`RNP` AS REAL)) FROM `Laboratory`))

question: For the patients followed at our thrombosis unit's outpatient clinic, what is the highest anti-ribonuclear protein value on record? I just need that single highest value for my review.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein (anti-RNP) is a blood antibody test result recorded for patients.
SQL: SELECT MAX(CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)) AS highest_anti_ribonuclear_protein_value FROM Laboratory AS l INNER JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-'

question: I'm studying patients who carry exactly the rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's syndrome overlap. Please look at each patient's own record and find those whose record names exactly rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's syndrome, in either order, and no other disease – a disease recorded only as suspected does not count as a diagnosis. For those patients, considering their whole recorded laboratory history regardless of date, I need two numbers: how many have had at least one laboratory result showing a normal platelet level, and how many have never had a laboratory result showing a normal platelet level – count a patient with no laboratory results at all as never having had a normal platelet result.
evidence: Rheumatoid arthritis is recorded as the code RA and Sjögren's syndrome as the code SJS. A normal platelet level means a platelet count above 100 and below 400.
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.PLT > 100 AND l.PLT < 400) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_normal_platelet_result, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.PLT > 100 AND l.PLT < 400) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS never_normal_platelet_result FROM Patient AS p WHERE LENGTH(LOWER(REPLACE(p.Diagnosis, ' ', ''))) - LENGTH(REPLACE(LOWER(REPLACE(p.Diagnosis, ' ', '')), ',', '')) = 1 AND REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(LOWER(REPLACE(p.Diagnosis, ' ', '')), 'ra', ''), 'sjs', ''), ',', '') = ''

question: I'm looking at patients whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody measurement came out higher than 32. Of those patients, how many were women and how many were men? Note that 'higher than 32' means strictly above 32, not equal to it, and a patient qualifies if any of their laboratory measurements exceeded 32.
evidence: A woman means a patient recorded as F, and a man means a patient recorded as M.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1.SEX = 'F' THEN T1.ID END) AS women, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1.SEX = 'M' THEN T1.ID END) AS men FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE CAST(T2.RNP AS REAL) > 32

question: For the patients in the registry with a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis, I'd like to know: (1) the total number of laboratory tests recorded for these patients, counting tests from all dates, and (2) how many of these patients have no laboratory tests recorded at all (i.e., patients with no laboratory record count as having no laboratory tests).
evidence: Psoriatic arthritis: a rheumatic disease diagnosis.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(l.ID) AS total_tests, SUM(CASE WHEN l.ID IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_test_patients FROM Patient p LEFT JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE LOWER(p.Diagnosis) = 'psoriatic arthritis'

question: I'm putting together a monitoring checklist for SLE patients. Among the thrombotic episodes recorded for patients diagnosed with SLE, which single symptom appears most frequently? I just need the symptom name back. Please count all recorded episodes with no date restriction. If two symptoms are equally frequent, give the one that comes first alphabetically. Note that a patient counts as having SLE only if their own diagnosis record names SLE among their diseases.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease. Thrombotic episode: an episode in which the patient experienced thrombosis.
SQL: WITH episodes AS (SELECT e.Symptoms FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE Instr(p.Diagnosis, 'SLE') > 0 AND e.Thrombosis > 0) SELECT Symptoms FROM episodes GROUP BY Symptoms HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM episodes GROUP BY Symptoms)) ORDER BY Symptoms LIMIT 1

question: In our autoimmune disease cohort, what percentage of thrombosis patients were diagnosed with SLE at the examination visit? I need the percentage on a 0-100 scale, rounded to two decimal places. Please use the diagnosis recorded at the examination visit, not the diagnosis on the patient's overall file. This is for a write-up on which diagnoses accompany thrombotic events in this cohort.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease; thrombosis: formation of a blood clot within a blood vessel
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN ID END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(DISTINCT ID), 2) AS percentage FROM Examination WHERE Thrombosis > 0

question: I'm reviewing thrombosis ward patients and need a chart-review list. Can you give me, for every patient who had a single lab visit where the panel showed both an LDH result strictly between 600 and 800 and urine protein of 300 mg/dL or more, the patient ID and their completed age in years as of 2026-10-09? If any one visit's panel shows both findings, that patient qualifies. Please note that a proteinuria result reported as "at least" a level counts at that stated level (e.g., "at least 300" counts as 300 mg/dL or more), and a plain number is in mg/dL. Nothing else needed, just patient ID and completed age.
evidence: Proteinuria result codes: '-' means negative, 'TR' means trace.
SQL: SELECT p.ID, CAST(SUBSTR('2026-10-09', 1, 4) AS INTEGER) - CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(p.Birthday AS CHAR(10)), 1, 4) AS INTEGER) - CASE WHEN SUBSTR('2026-10-09', 6, 5) < SUBSTR(CAST(p.Birthday AS CHAR(10)), 6, 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS age FROM Patient AS p WHERE p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.LDH > 600 AND l.LDH < 800 AND CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(CAST(l.`U-PRO` AS TEXT), '>', ''), '=', '') AS REAL) >= 300) ORDER BY p.ID

question: I'm reviewing our cohort and need to identify patients whose most recent laboratory sample on file was collected after 1 January 1997 (strictly later than that date) and whose most recent anti-Scl-70 result on file was normal. Please return only the patient IDs for these patients.
evidence: anti-Scl-70: anti-topoisomerase I antibody, an autoantibody measured in the laboratory. A normal anti-Scl-70 result is a result of 'negative' or 0.
SQL: WITH lab AS (SELECT ID, MAX(Date) AS LastDate FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), last_sc AS (SELECT s.ID AS ID, s.SC170 AS SC170 FROM Laboratory s WHERE s.SC170 IS NOT NULL AND s.Date = (SELECT MAX(s2.Date) FROM Laboratory s2 WHERE s2.ID = s.ID AND s2.SC170 IS NOT NULL)) SELECT l.ID FROM lab l JOIN last_sc c ON c.ID = l.ID WHERE l.LastDate > '1997-01-01' AND c.SC170 IN ('negative','0') ORDER BY l.ID

question: I'd like to know how many patients on record have both an abnormal anti-SSA antibody result and a positive proteinuria finding at some point in their record. Abnormal anti-SSA means any recorded test result other than negative or zero. Proteinuria counts as positive if any urine test on file returned a result other than negative or none. The two findings don't need to come from the same visit – I'm looking across each patient's entire record. Please just give me the number of such patients.
evidence: anti-SSA: anti-SSA antibody laboratory test; proteinuria: protein found in the urine
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS T1 WHERE T1.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE SSA IS NOT NULL AND SSA NOT IN ('negative', '0')) AND T1.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` IS NOT NULL AND `U-PRO` NOT IN ('-', '0'))

question: Among patients in the thrombosis prediction database whose creatinine level is normal (below 1.5), what is the highest anti-RNP antibody level recorded? Please return just that single number; if several measurements tie for the highest, the tied value is the answer.
evidence: Anti-RNP antibody = anti-ribonuclear protein antibody, measured by the laboratory panel.
SQL: SELECT MAX(CAST(T2.RNP AS REAL)) AS max_rnp_level FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.CRE < 1.5

question: I'd like to see how severe anemia is distributed across the sexes in the registry. Please give me, for each sex, the number of patients of that sex who ever showed severe anemia on any lab test, with the rows labeled 'female' and 'male'.
evidence: Severe anemia means a hemoglobin value below 7.0 g/dL on a lab test.
SQL: SELECT CASE p.SEX WHEN 'F' THEN 'female' WHEN 'M' THEN 'male' END AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS severe_anemia_patients FROM Patient AS p INNER JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.HGB < 7.0 GROUP BY p.SEX HAVING p.SEX IN ('F','M')

question: For patients whose sex is not recorded in the registry, I need two counts for the annual quality report: how many have at least one laboratory result on file, and of those, how many have at least one laboratory result showing elevated total bilirubin. The report covers all dates.
evidence: A patient's sex is not recorded when the registry holds no sex entry for that patient. Total bilirubin of 2.0 or higher counts as elevated.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T2.ID) AS patients_with_lab_results, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.`T-BIL` >= 2.0 THEN T2.ID END) AS patients_with_elevated_bilirubin FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.SEX IS NULL OR T1.SEX = ''

question: For an audit, I need the number of admitted female patients born between 1945 and 1989 (inclusive) who have an ANA examination where the observed pattern is exactly P, with no other pattern alongside it. Please return just that single count.
evidence: ANA pattern: the pattern observed in the ANA examination, e.g. 'P' or 'P,S'; the admission mark starting with a plus indicates the patient was admitted.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Examination AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.Admission LIKE '+%' AND T1.SEX = 'F' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) BETWEEN '1945' AND '1989' AND T2.`ANA Pattern` = 'P'

question: I'm screening the thrombosis cohort for a follow-up panel. Can you give me the patient ids of outpatients (patients followed at the outpatient clinic rather than admitted) whose creatinine phosphokinase is in the normal range (below 250) but whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level is above 4 (strictly greater than 4)? Please note that an anti-ribonuclear protein result reported as negative means no antibody was detected. I just need the patient ids, nothing else.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.CPK < 250 AND T1.Admission = '-' AND CAST(T2.RNP AS REAL) > 4

question: I'm trying to size a subgroup in the thrombosis cohort: how many female patients had a normal prothrombin time (below 14 seconds) along with an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein level (16 or higher)? Please use the prothrombin time and anti-ribonuclear protein level from the same laboratory record for each patient. I just need the count of such female patients.
evidence: Normal prothrombin time: below 14 seconds. Elevated anti-ribonuclear protein: a measured level of 16 or higher.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.SEX = 'F' AND T2.PT < 14 AND CAST(T2.RNP AS REAL) >= 16

question: I need to find lupus patients with liver lab abnormalities. Can you give me the ID and sex of every patient who has at least one total bilirubin (T-BIL) result at or above the upper normal limit of 1.2 mg/dL, and who has a confirmed diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)? SLE counts if it's among the patient's confirmed diagnoses, even when other diseases are diagnosed or suspected alongside it, but a suspected SLE alone doesn't count. The diagnosis should be the patient's overall diagnosis, not something noted at a single examination. Please order results by sex, then patient ID, and return only the ID and sex.
evidence: T-BIL: total bilirubin; SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus; susp.: suspected, not a confirmed diagnosis
SQL: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX FROM Patient AS p WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE "T-BIL" >= 1.2) AND instr(',' || REPLACE(p.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',' || 'SLE' || ',') > 0 ORDER BY p.SEX, p.ID;

question: Among all patients diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus, I want to find the patient whose anti-DNA test result was the strongest ever recorded for that disease. Please report the patient's identifier, the patient's diagnosis, and that patient's highest anti-DNA test result, using the number exactly as the test wrote it. If several patients tie for the highest anti-DNA result, list every tied patient.
evidence: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease; anti-DNA is an antibody test reported as a number.
SQL: WITH ranked AS (SELECT p.ID AS patient_id, p.Diagnosis AS diagnosis, l.DNA AS highest_anti_dna, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) DESC, l.Date DESC) AS rn FROM Patient p INNER JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL), best AS (SELECT patient_id, diagnosis, highest_anti_dna FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1) SELECT patient_id, diagnosis, highest_anti_dna FROM best WHERE CAST(highest_anti_dna AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(highest_anti_dna AS REAL)) FROM best) ORDER BY patient_id

question: For our thrombosis study cohort, I'd like to know how often patients have a normal IgG status at their most recent check, broken down by care setting. Please give me, for patients admitted to the hospital and for patients followed at the outpatient clinic, the percentage of that setting's patients whose most recent IgG measurement was normal. The percentage should be out of every patient in that setting, so patients who never had an IgG measurement count toward the denominator but not the numerator. Please round to one decimal place, and label the two results exactly as 'admitted to the hospital' and 'followed at the outpatient clinic'.
evidence: An IgG measurement is considered normal when it is above 900 and below 2000.
SQL: WITH latest AS (SELECT ID, IGG, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date DESC) AS rn FROM Laboratory WHERE IGG IS NOT NULL) SELECT CASE WHEN p.Admission = '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.IGG > 900 AND l.IGG < 2000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(p.ID), 1) AS patient_share FROM Patient AS p LEFT JOIN latest AS l ON l.ID = p.ID AND l.rn = 1 WHERE p.Admission IN ('+', '-') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

question: In the thrombosis prediction cohort, I want to gauge how often the most recent anti-ribonuclear protein measurement among female patients was markedly elevated while CPK stayed low at that same measurement. Please give me a single integer: the number of female patients whose most recent anti-ribonuclear protein titer was above 64 and whose CPK from that same laboratory record was below 250. Above 64 means strictly greater than 64, and below 250 means strictly less than 250.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein is an autoantibody measured as a titer in the blood; a negative result means the antibody was not detected.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS female_patients FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.Date = (SELECT MAX(l2.Date) FROM Laboratory AS l2 WHERE l2.ID = p.ID AND l2.RNP IS NOT NULL) AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 64 AND l.CPK < 250

question: I'm summarizing anti-cardiolipin IgM levels for lupus patients. What was the average anti-cardiolipin IgM concentration across examinations performed between 1993-10-01 and 1993-10-31 (both days inclusive) in which systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) was diagnosed? Please round the average to 1 decimal place.
evidence: SLE = systemic lupus erythematosus
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(e."aCL IgM"), 1) AS avg_aCL_IgM FROM Examination AS e WHERE e."Examination Date" BETWEEN '1993-10-01' AND '1993-10-31' AND instr(',' || REPLACE(e.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',' || 'SLE' || ',') > 0

question: Among the patients who have laboratory test records on file, how many are female and how many are male? Please give me one line for the female patients and one line for the male patients, each showing the sex and the number of patients of that sex.
SQL: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX IN ('F','M') GROUP BY p.SEX

question: Which patients followed at the outpatient clinic have both an abnormal red blood cell count and a positive anti-ribonuclear protein antibody result? Please return the patient IDs. Note: the two findings don't need to be from the same laboratory visit - a patient qualifies if at least one lab test shows an abnormal RBC and at least one, possibly different, lab test shows a positive anti-ribonuclear protein antibody. Here, a positive anti-ribonuclear protein antibody means a titer above zero, an abnormal RBC means RBC <= 3.5 or RBC >= 6.0, and outpatient follow-up means Admission = '-'.
SQL: SELECT T1.ID FROM Patient T1 WHERE T1.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory L1 WHERE L1.ID = T1.ID AND (L1.RBC <= 3.5 OR L1.RBC >= 6)) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory L2 WHERE L2.ID = T1.ID AND CAST(L2.RNP AS REAL) > 0) ORDER BY T1.ID
